pages.title: Galapagos Giant Tortoise
pages.text: The Galápagos giant tortoise ($(o)Chelonoidis niger$()) is the largest living tortoise. Each of the Galápagos Islands has its own form, and many scientists now treat them as separate species.$(br2)Tortoises from moist highlands have big domed shells, while those from dry islands have saddle-shaped shells raised at the front, so they can stretch their long necks up to cactus pads.$(br2)The islands' vice-governor told Charles Darwin he could tell which island a tortoise came from by its shell.
